intro: For hundreds of years, most Europeans were born into a rank they could not easily leave. A serf's child became a serf. A noble's child became a noble. Then plague, towns, revolutions and machines began to shake that order loose. In this unit you will follow those changes from the medieval manor to the industrial city.

You will meet knights swearing oaths, barons facing down a king, and French commoners swearing an oath on a tennis court. You will stand inside a Manchester cotton mill and read the words of Adam Smith, Karl Marx and their critics. Each group saw fairness in its own way, and you will hear from all of them.

By the end, you will be able to explain how social class worked in Europe, name the events that changed it, and compare big ideas about work and wealth. You will use evidence to make your own claim, and you will treat people who disagree with care.
bigQuestion: What decides a person's place in society, and how have people worked to change it?

timeline.t: Writers describe society as those who pray, fight and work
English barons force King John to accept Magna Carta
The Black Death kills a huge share of Europe's people
Richard Arkwright opens his water-powered mill at Cromford
Adam Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations
Tennis Court Oath; France ends the three estates
British Factory Act limits children's hours in textile mills
Marx and Engels publish The Communist Manifesto
Germany under Bismarck begins national health insurance

words.d: a system where land was given in exchange for loyalty and military service
a peasant bound to a lord's land who owed labor but was not owned like a slave
one of the three ranks of society: clergy, nobility and commoners
the 1215 charter that limited the power of King John of England
an association of people in one trade that set rules, prices and training
a special right given to one group and not to others
the shift from hand-made goods to machine-made goods in factories, starting in Britain
people who earn their living mainly by selling their labor for wages
the group between the wealthy and the working class, such as owners and professionals
an organization of workers who bargain together with employers
an economic system where private people own businesses and trade for profit
a system where the government helps protect people against sickness, injury and old age

test.q: In feudalism, what did a vassal promise a lord?
test.why: Vassals swore loyalty and owed military service in return for a fief.

test.q: Which estate was the largest in France in 1789?
test.why: The Third Estate was about 98 percent of the population.

test.q: What was one result of the Black Death?
choices: The start of the factory system
A labor shortage that let workers ask for higher pay
test.why: So many died that surviving workers were scarce and could ask for more.

test.q: What idea is Magna Carta best known for?
choices: Even the king is under the law
The Church should have no land
test.why: Magna Carta put limits on the king's power under the law.

test.q: What were the steps to becoming a master in a guild?
test.why: Guild members trained as apprentices, worked as journeymen, then became masters.

test.q: What did the Tennis Court Oath promise?
choices: To obey the king in all things
Not to separate until France had a constitution
test.why: The deputies swore to stay together until France had a written constitution.

test.q: Which document said men are born and remain free and equal in rights?
choices: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
test.why: Article 1 of the 1789 Declaration said this.

test.q: Why did the Industrial Revolution begin in Britain?
choices: Coal, capital, trade and inventors came together there
test.why: Historians point to coal and iron, capital, trade and inventors.

test.q: What did the Sadler Committee's testimony show?
choices: Children worked very long, hard hours in mills
test.why: Workers described long days, beatings and injuries.

choices: A new kind of spinning machine
Workers stopping work together to press demands
test.why: In a strike, workers stop work together to press for better pay or conditions.

test.q: What did Adam Smith see in the pin factory?
choices: The division of labor raised output greatly
test.why: Smith saw that splitting pin-making into steps made far more pins.

test.q: What did Marx and Engels predict?
test.why: They predicted workers would rise up and create a communist society.

test.q: Which is a real record critics point to about states built in Marx's name?
test.why: Under Stalin, millions were sent to the Gulag camps.

test.q: What was one reason Bismarck created social insurance?
choices: To win workers away from socialists
test.why: Bismarck hoped insurance would draw workers away from socialism.

test.q: How was a factory worker's life like a serf's, and how was it different?
choices: Both were free from all work
Both worked for others, but the worker earned wages and could change jobs
test.why: Serfs were tied to land; workers were tied to wages but could legally move.

write.prompt: Which change did more to loosen the hold of birth on a person's place in society: the French Revolution or the Industrial Revolution? Make a claim. Support it with two or three facts or sources from this unit, and explain one fair point on the other side.
tips: State your claim in one clear sentence.
Name your sources, such as the Declaration of 1789 or the Factory Act of 1833.
Use unit terms like estate, privilege, working class and middle class.
Give the other side fairly before you answer it.
